Synopsis:
The player has stolen a most sacred idol from the druids.Though the druids have made peace with the players and the tieflings at this time, they can't let anyone steal their idol, so they interrogate the player when they see him.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_NGB_GroveConflict_IdolCrime.json: The player has already taken the Idol of Silvanus from the druids, and druids — though at peace with the player and nearby tieflings — confront and interrogate them because the theft cannot be ignored. Off-screen, witnesses or guards may be present (a goblin child who saw looting, Zhent-style agents by a chest, or Mol’s gang/guards in the Den), so this exchange can be a crime-trigger reaction drawn from those clusters. The player’s available responses include denying knowledge, confessing, threatening or attacking, and prior choices (being seen looting, trespassing, or crossing Mol) affect how NPCs respond. Sample outcomes shown include the player admitting and violently threatening the druids to be allowed to leave, or choosing to attack.

context: The player has already stolen the Idol of Silvanus, and although the druids are currently at peace with the party and nearby tieflings, they must confront anyone who takes their sacred idol. This exchange is a crime-trigger interrogation: druids (sometimes with off-screen witnesses or guards — e.g., a goblin child, Zhent-style agents, or Mol’s gang) press the player about the theft, and prior choices like being seen looting or trespassing affect their response. The player's available moves include denying, confessing, threatening, or attacking; example outcomes show either a violent threat letting the player leave or an outright attack. This scene pulls from the Grove Conflict and general interrogation clusters and represents one possible resolution, not every branching result.
